levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The conclusion is stated as certain when the scenario does not support that.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Uncertainty is mentioned in general terms only.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known and how it limits the conclusion.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known, how it limits the conclusion, and what would resolve it.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Some criteria are used and others are dropped without saying why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: Every stated criterion is applied and the result of each is reported.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: Every criterion is applied and the response says which one decided the outcome.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

judgment.prompt: Vehicle B ends with the most money, but Vehicle A is the only one of the three a saver can reach at any time without giving anything up. Argue for one of them for money that has a 1-in-4 chance of being needed inside the two years, and name what your choice costs.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Chooses either A or B and defends it with the $36.49 difference between their ending balances against the cost of not being able to reach Vehicle B for 24 months.
Names what the choice gives up specifically — either the $36.49 of extra interest, or the ability to take the money out during the lock period.
Treats the stated 1-in-4 chance as the fact that decides the question rather than assuming the money will or will not be needed.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $5,418.41 and $5,454.90 ending balances, and refers to the 24-month lock on Vehicle B.
lookFors: Either choice is fully defensible here; what is being scored is whether the cost of the choice is named.
The response does not select Vehicle C on the strength of its 4.75% headline, having computed the $96.00 of fees.
judgment.commonMisconception: Ranking savings vehicles by advertised yield without netting out flat fees or pricing the access restriction.
